utterances.text: Yes. It went on during the meeting itself. Also, it was very complex and the intensity of the operation was quite considerable. This began in late August and went on into September. The intensity of the operations, according to the reports that I had -- I wasn't there in Mostar, so during the war, I never entered the encircled Mostar, but what I had in information from the Supreme Command Staff and directly from contacts with the late General Arif Pasalic is that the enemy activities in that area of Mostar was quite intense. That was the part that was under the control of the B and H army.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Gusic, I'm going to come back to you for detail about each of these matters, but at the moment I just want to get a broad chronology, if that's okay. Now, after the -- on or about the 29th of August - and I'm not putting a specific date to you now to remember after these many years - but at the end of August, an inspection team arrived in your area consisting of Mr. Suljevic, Mr. Bilajac, Mr. Karic, and Mr. Dzankovic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Generals Suljevic, Bilajac, and Brigadier Vehbija Karic, I did see them, but I did not see Dzankovic. They stopped by at my forward command post. And not only that. They stopped by to see me quite often at the command. These were the generals who most -- who most often came to see me. These were the generals, Bilajac and Suljevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: On or about the 1st of September, Sefer Halilovic arrived to take up team leadership in that team; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot know the exact date. I cannot tell you the exact date. But it's true that in early September General Halilovic came to that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: There's a journalist called Sevko Hodzic who is to give evidence, we believe, in this case at a later time. If Sevko Hodzic took good notes of the dates when he met you and other operatives, are you in a position to dispute the accuracy of -- I'm not referring to the accuracy of everything he says happened but the accuracy of the dates that he ascribes.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: With reference to the writings of Sevko Hodzic, I cannot confirm anything. I do not have a good opinion of his writings, but I have no reason to doubt the dates he mentions. However, I feel that his way of writing is improper and that he makes comments he is not qualified to make because he doesn't have sufficient knowledge, at least military knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well -- well, Mr. Morrissey, when you mention a person, please do not say that -- whether that person is going to testify or not because at this moment we have no idea whether there's any request for the -- for the protective measures.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I apologise for that. I was really endeavouring -- well, there's an excuse, but you don't need to hear it. I'm sorry, Your Honour. I'm endeavour to do better.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. And on the 4th of September, Rasim Delic, the commander of the army, arrived in Herzegovina and spent the night in Konjic, where your base also was; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He didn't spend the night in the corps command. He spent the night in another building. It was a JNA building. I cannot say that that was the date, but it's true that it was within the first ten days of September that General Delic was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: The following day from that -- from that day, the 5th of September, you attended at a meeting of commanders, including Sefer Halilovic and Selmo Cikotic and other commanders, at a village called Dobro Polje; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the precise date, but it's true there was a meeting at Dobro Polje. Brigadier Cikotic was there, the commander of the independent battalion, Enver Buza, was there; the commander of the 317th, the late Enver Zejnilagic was there, Haso Hakalovic was there; the commander of the Sutjeska Battalion was there; Brigadier Vehbija Karic was there; General Bilajac was there; I think General Zicro Suljevic was there as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Had you met Vehbija Karic before?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I knew him from 1992 in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Was he a married man?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know he had a son. But whether he was married, I don't know. I did meet his son on Igman -- or at least, he introduced himself as Vehbija Karic's son. He was a young man who introduced himself as Vehbija Karic's son. As to whether he was married, believe me, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, let me just see if you can exercise your memory on that. Was he married to a Croatian woman?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you I didn't know whether he was married at all. I don't know about that, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. To your knowledge - and I'm talking about knowledge that you've acquired later on - were citizens killed in Grabovica on the night of the 8th and the morning of the 9th of September 1993?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I learnt that a crime had been committed in Grabovica, but to this day I cannot say that I know the exact date when this was done. I was never on the scene of the crime, and I cannot say whether it was on the 9th or the 8th or on some other day. I do know that two or three days later, between the 12th and the 15th, I got this information from Nermin Eminovic, my assistant for security.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you. On the 13th of September, was there an attack launched by Bosnian army units towards Makiljen [phoen] and in the area of Crni Vrh - that's C-r-n-i V-r-h - and I apologise for any massacre of the pronunciation.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't have this information because I wasn't involved in those combat operations. I don't know the date when it was launched. I know that there were combat operations on that axis, but I don't know when they were launched.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, if the evidence proves that -- if other evidence proves that it was the 13th of September that the 317th Brigade and some attached units went into battle in that area, you would not be disputing that date; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: How can I dispute it when I don't know the date? I can neither dispute it nor confirm it. I don't know the date when it was launched.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. And on -- but what you can say is that on the day following that, the Prozor Independent Battalion went into an attack in the vicinity of the villages in Uzdol; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you whether it was on that day or the day before or the day after. I wasn't in charge of those combat operations, and I don't know when it happened. But I do know that the Prozor Battalion was active on that axis. I know that. The general direction, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Well, I understand that's your position. Now, on the -- on the 16th, you received an order from Stjepan Siber indicating that the cease-fire had been clinched in Geneva; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And that's --

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 16th.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I cut you off. Pardon me.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 16th, all the units received that order, not just the 6th Corps. All the units and all the elements of the Supreme Command Staff received this order.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. And that order included a requirement that all combat activity cease by the 18th; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that's correct, yes. To cease offensive combat operations. I believe that defensive actions were never in any doubt, but all offensive actions were to be halted.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: To your recollection, did the HVO cease its activities on the 18th of -- of September and stop firing bullets into Mostar?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't reply to that question with any precision because, as I said, I never went to Mostar. The information I received was that combat operations did not stop. However, whether it was the HVO or the Army of BH that did not stop combat operations, I don't know. I cannot confirm this because I was never there. So I cannot say who failed to stop their combat operations, which side.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, in the week -- you're aware that -- we'll come to that later. You're aware that -- that Sefer Halilovic went back to Sarajevo on approximately the 19th or -- I'm not asking you -- I'm not asking you to be precise about it, but you know that Sefer Halilovic returned to Sarajevo very soon after that date, the 18th?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the precise date, but whether it was in October or September, I don't know. But it's true that at some point, not very long after the end of combat operations, General Halilovic did go to Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Now, I want just to clinch a matter that was raised earlier on, which I want to conclude now, and it's a matter that arises at that end period of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown a document, it's Defence Rule 65 ter number D104; Defence ERN number DD00.04 -- 0420. It's marked for identification 132 or going to be marked ultimately.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see only the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: While that's being brought up, can I just -- I'll raise one matter with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: This is a correspondence from the accused man, Mr. Halilovic, to Rasim Delic. And once you've looked at it, I'm going to ask you to confirm whether you've -- and drawn your attention particularly to one part of it, I'm going to ask you whether you've seen the document and I'm going to ask you whether you remember the incident. Do you now have the -- the Bosnian version of that in front of you?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not yet. Not yet. It's here now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you please look to the second indented paragraph, which commences with the words: "Although with your permission, I said to Salko Gusic..." Do you have that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Would you read it and I'll read with you, that Sefer Halilovic says there: "Although with your permission, I said to Salko Gusic, the commander of the 6th Corps, that we would see each other in Jablanica on Saturday, he has not shown up yet or contacted me. This has become his habit. I was looking for him in the area of responsibility of the 6th Corps for four or five days, and then met him by chance in the command of the 6th Corps. If Pisvir is lost, then Jablanica and the valley of the Neretva would be very difficult to defend. He seems to have taken it very seriously that I cannot order him, which is basically what I do not want. However, it would be only fitting if he or someone else from the corps command at least contacted me because there is fierce fighting going on here." Have you read and understand -- have you read now in this court and understood that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did any investigators or any other person ever show you that document to comment on?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never commented on this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Do you agree with the allegations that Sefer Halilovic was making, that you wouldn't talk to him and that you took it very seriously that he could not command you? Do you agree with what he said when he said it back in September of 1993?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot agree with this. I can't believe that General Halilovic would write this. Somebody probably wrote this on his behalf. I won't say he didn't sign it, but somebody else must have drafted this for him. This is not correct. It could be true that we didn't meet, but had he told me we had to meet, we would have met, or at least we would have talked by some means of communication. That he had to go looking for me in my area of responsibility for four or five days, well, everybody knew where I was. I was at the forward command post in Fojnica. If I had received a message, I would have gone to see him. Anyone from the corps command - for example, my deputy - hadn't he gone to the meeting in Buturovic Polje? He was authorised to make decisions on my behalf.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Could the witness now please be shown another document. Perhaps I offer that document as well. The next document that I would wish the witness to be shown is Defence document D17 -- Defence Rule 65 ter number D17; Defence ERN number DD00.0055; MFI133.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I have the full screen on this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Do you now have that document, Mr. Gusic?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. I'm reading it. Can you give me a moment to read it through?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'll read it with you. Is it -- is it addressed to the chief of Sjever, Sefer Halilovic personally, and to the commander -- the command of the 6th Corps, the commander personally? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Does it recite that: "We received a document from Mr. Sefer Halilovic in which he states that among other things he did not manage to find you although he had an appointment with you at Jablanica on the 30th of September, 1993 and for this reason I hereby order..." and Rasim Delic goes on to order certain things. Is that the fact?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, did you complain to Rasim Delic that this was an unjustified complaint by Sefer Halilovic and that you weren't failing to meet him at all? Or is the answer to that "never"?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I contacted the commander after receiving this order and told him I never knew about the meeting scheduled for the 30th of September. I never knew about it. And when I received this document, that was the first time I saw that an appointment had been scheduled. There were ways in which I could have been informed that this meeting had been planned and that I was supposed to attend it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Mr. Gusic, from that you now acknowledge receiving this document from Rasim Delic, don't you?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This document stuck in my mind because of what it says that further combat activities should not be carried out without the commander's approval because there was an order on cease-fire. So that's why this document sticks in my memory.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did it stick in your memory yesterday?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yesterday? It wasn't shown to me yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, I tender that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I just want to ask you -- I'm sorry, I just want to ask one further question about the -- one further topic about that. Would you look, please, to document number -- sorry, to prong number 4.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I just --

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Delivered to the commander --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... to you. I put to you that there, just as on the map that's behind you, a person who's the commander of the Operation Neretva 93 is made perfectly explicit in the form of an order and that that person was none other than the commander of the army, Rasim Delic.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what you say. I cannot confirm this. I don't want to deny it. I'm not denying for a single moment that somebody else was perhaps commanding the operation, but I have no proof of that. I know who was the commander at the forward command post. I know who directly issued tasks to the units on the ground. And whether that's someone -- not someone but General Halilovic. Whether he had to consult General Delic about each one of his decisions and receive approval from him, it was not General Halilovic's duty to inform me of this nor can I claim to know about it. But from what you are showing me here, this does not refer to the Neretva operation but, rather, to the preparations that I was ordered to carry out, and in connection with these preparations I was to submit reports to General Delic. In other words, I was to report to him on how the preparations were going and in what manner.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Are you suggesting that Neretva 93 had finished by this time?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. I am not saying it was finished.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: What combat -- what combat operations were you planning and preparing in Herzegovina with the chief of the Sjever, Sefer Halilovic personally, to which General Delic refers if not Neretva 93? What other combat activities in the area of General Halilovic's Neretva 93, as you would have it, were being prepared?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Defensive operations. It was necessary to defend the positions we were holding in order to avoid a fiasco because of the lack of success of the operations that were being carried out.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Have a look at number -- paragraph 4 again, please.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... reference to defensive operations or is it in truth a reference to offensive operations?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Paragraph 4?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, paragraph 4 and none other.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Four?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, four. Is that a reference in your account to defensive operations or, rather, is it a reference to offensive operations?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment. This can refer either to offensive or to defensive activities. Let me remind you that a defence can be flexible and that there can be offensive activities with smaller units in certain directions, which doesn't mean that this is an offensive activity. It's aimed at maintaining the positions we are already holding. One can't say that this couldn't refer to large-scale offensive operations, but I know that after this order we did not prepare any large-scale offensive operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: But it's your -- you're the one who says here - and I just want to clarify this - you're the one who says this is not -- this order is not connected to Neretva 93. And I'm asking you to specify what offensive operations, if any, this order refers to if not offensive operations within Neretva 93. Could you clarify that, please. If it's not Neretva 93, what is it?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This order doesn't have to be an order within the framework of the Operation Neretva 93. If command of the operation were taken over by the commander who would introduce new forces, which he's doing here, he could either order combat activities within this operation or open up a new operation. I personally think that this order cannot prove that this is a continuation of the Operation Neretva 93 but it cannot prove that preparations were not being made to create the conditions for a continuation of combat operations. The goal of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina was the liberation of the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina. This was a permanent task. And we always had to prepare our units for offensive operations. In this particular case, there is an axis or a direction that is given and an idea or a plan that we had to prepare for.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: One final question arising out of this document, and then we're going to go back to the start and we'll work through in a more chronological way than I have currently been doing. What you can say is that looking at that order there is no doubt that by the time of the issuing of that order, on the 1st of October, 1993, there was potential offensive conduct in Herzegovina being planned and prepared that was not part of Neretva 93; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the last part of your question. I haven't really understood it very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: The last part was "is that correct," but I'll put the question again to you just to make sure that -- to be fair. The question was this --

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And I'll put it in the precise terms I put it. By the time of the issuing of that order, which you have, on the 1st of October 1993, there was potential offensive conduct in Herzegovina being planned and prepared that was not part of Neretva 93; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Potential activities -- planned potential activities is something that did not happen. But from this order there was the instruction to plan potential activities. So in my opinion, it was pointing in the direction of planning new other combat activities, but still it's difficult to assess whether these are offensive or defensive combat operations, but I think that we're talking about a series of minor strikes in order to achieve the desired possessions. But outside of Neretva 93 at that time, I cannot confirm that there were any other combat operations, but work was underway in planning new combat operations or even to continue combat operations as part of Neretva 93. But I would just like to note -- or perhaps I'm commenting on something that I should not be commenting on, but if the combat operations as part of Neretva 93 were to continue, after an order like this it would be inevitable for the commander himself to assume command since this order emanated from him, if activities were to continue, further activities within the framework of Neretva 93. I think that it would be improper to leave a person to do something, but we were already interfering in his area of responsibility and limiting his work by beginning new operations. He should be permitted to finish, from start to finish, what he began. But the commander was the one who would continue when these operations would continue, if there were to be operations -- further operations as part of Neretva 93. And at that stage, the stage of the order, following the order then the commander should be the one who would assume or should assume command.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you for that, Mr. Gusic. I take it you've noticed who the commander is in relation to this order. Yes?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand who the commander -- you mean the Supreme Command Staff commander?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... the order as commander. That was Rasim Delic, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Rasim Delic is the commander of the Supreme Command Staff of the Armed Forces of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and this order is addressed to General Halilovic and myself. Therefore, because I did not up to that point participate in these combat operations - I was being tasked to begin preparations or to join the preparations - probably the commander had some new idea which could be different from the one that we can see here on the map. That is possible. But it could also be the same concept. So I don't know what the commander's idea was before he drafted this order, because this is a preparatory order. That's the form it's given in. It's not an order that meant that we were to begin implementation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you again. Do you see there any sign of the order being directed to an IKM or sent to an IKM?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could I please just look at the beginning of the document, because I only have the places that the order is supposed to be delivered to. So I would just like it to be -- I would like to see a little bit down on the page. Could you please just scroll it up a little bit more. I would like to look at the end of the document, please. The only thing that would indicate that it was sent to the IKM would be the stamp of the communications centre that received it and that in the heading it is also addressed to General Halilovic. These are two indications which would tell me that -- that this document was sent to the IKM. The document was received at the IKM at 22.45 hours on the 1st of October.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: You're referring to the part that's shown on the screen there, are you? Do you have on the screen there the stamp?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And what -- what -- you don't see the words "IKM" there, do you? You see: "C-OP Jablanica; correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you can see "The Jablanica communications centre."

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. Your Honours, I tender MFI132 and MFI133. Both are for tender.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Gusic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we could, you know, consider the admission of the documents at this stage or we could do it later on, because I believe that there are a bunch of the documents on the side of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Pardon me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Who has not been tendered yet. So -- so maybe you could do it all together at the end.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Now, Mr. Gusic, I'm going to now take you back to Zenica and the meeting at Zenica. Very well. Now, the meeting at Zenica, I put to you, was a very important meeting for the leadership of the army of Rasim Delic and indeed was the first occasion when he had assembled all of the corps commanders together to discuss future directions for the war. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And when you attended, apart from the people that you mentioned as being present yesterday, also in attendance was the Minister of the Interior, an individual named Bakir Alispaic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember. I dare not say that he was or that he wasn't. When I was preparing for the testimony, I saw a video clip in Sarajevo perhaps about half a year ago, and I can't recall seeing him. Since there is a video recording, if I see -- saw him on that recording, perhaps I -- then, of course, it would indicate that he was there. But I really cannot remember whether he was there or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. That raises the issue of the tape. At the time when that meeting took place, it was videotaped and audiotaped, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: When you were shown the videotape -- sorry, I shouldn't shouldn't say "videotape." You were shown a DVD, weren't you, by the investigators?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I saw a DVD. It was on DVD. I looked at that recording in Sarajevo on the Office of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And one thing you did at that time was to point out to the investigators that a significant portion of that tape at the end was missing; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. I think that the meeting did not conclude in the way it -- that can be seen on that recording because tasks were issued at the end. There was a brief address by the commander with specific and concise tasks, and I didn't see that on this recording. And not only that. I told the investigator also that a part of the tape that was in -- showing some part of the meeting, there was a lot that I recall that certain people said which is not on the tape. So this is -- in the course of the tape, you can see that not everything that each person said is on the tape. This is what I told the investigator at the time. I think that what I said is almost entirely recorded, but I can't claim that with 100 per cent certainty. But I did refer to certain statements by those who spoke before me, and I don't remember hearing some of the things they said or seeing that on the tape. I know that I referred to the statement by the late General Arif Pasalic, and I don't remember hearing him say that on the tape.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. I'm going to take you to some specific questions about the tape, but there are some questions I want to put to you about the substance of the -- of what was said. You can confirm, I take it, the following facts: No such -- sorry, I take that back. No Operation Neretva 93 was mentioned at all; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The name of the operation was never mentioned. I did not hear it mentioned at the meeting. I did not hear the term "Neretva 93" mentioned at the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: The next point: Sefer Halilovic offered no plan at that meeting for an operation related to Mostar or indeed related to Herzegovina at all; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, no, he didn't. Not as an operation, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: In fact, in a statement that you made to the Prosecutors recently, the most recent statement that you made -- you made the comment that the -- that -- I'll read it to you: "Listening to the statements of General Sefer Halilovic during the meeting and on the recording, I can see that his main focus was the warehouse in Zemunica, Hadzici, and an explosives factory in Vitez, Vitez being the priority. General Halilovic did not even mention Mostar. The situation in Mostar was presented by General Arif Pasalic." And that's what you said to the -- to the investigators and that was the truth; correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. And on that -- at that meeting, no one was appointed to command an operation in Herzegovina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I recall, that is correct; no one was appointed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Mr. Gusic, I understand it's a very long time ago, and should you need or feel the need to read a transcript or even to look at the tape, it may be possible that that opportunity to be furnished and we'd come back to question you about it at a different time; not to play you lengthy slabs of tape in this court. But I just want to make it clear that if that is your position, you indicate it and we'll see. Now, you don't know yourself who it was who caused the parts of the tape which are missing to go missing, do you?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't. The first time I saw the tape was on the premises of the Tribunal in Sarajevo. I didn't view the tape prior to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Certainly. Now,--

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And just one more thing: I am not claiming that somebody removed those parts. It's possible that the person who was actually taping it at the time did not tape everything. So I'm not going into the reasons why he would tape certain things and not other things. But based on what I saw, it's not a complete tape, I believe, and not all the particulars are depicted on the tape that took place on that day in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Now, I'm going to press on to ask you certain details of what was said by individuals, particularly Commander Delic, you, and briefly Arif Pasalic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Morrissey, before you go into details, is this the right time for us to take a break?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. And we'll take a 20-minute break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Morrissey. Let's go into details.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Gusic, there's a document that -- a document that I think the Prosecution used yesterday, MFI109. This is a document referred to as the Zenica conclusions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I wonder if the witness could be shown the Zenica conclusions, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Mr. Gusic, while that's being arranged for you, I just indicate I'm going to take you to a couple of the comments made in those conclusions by Rasim Delic and ask for your comment on a couple of matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could we please have the following page. Do we need a page number?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Now, I won't ask you to comment on the knife in the back line there, but do you see a line beginning "The HVO attack ..."? It's four lines from the top, I think you'll find.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're talking about item 4, if I understand you properly, or ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I was going to talk about item 4, but, Mr. Gusic, you have anticipated the question. However, could I just ask you to confirm something about items 2 and 3, first of all. Mr. Gusic, I should say this, that in this Tribunal it's not permissible to ask questions about who is in the right and who is in the wrong in wars, and it's simply not relevant to the determination. But I have got some questions for you about your perception and the shared perception so far as you understood it of the army as to the dangers being faced by the Bosniak people and the Bosnian people, not just Bosniak but Bosnian generally. First of all, in the Bosnian army, were there numerous Croats fighting?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know about numerous, but in the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina there were Croats. I don't know what the percentage would be, but there were Croats, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Was Stjepan Siber, the deputy commander, a Croat?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how he -- what his ethnicity is, how he declares himself, but I think that he was a Croat. I think he is a Croat. I don't know how he feels, which group he belongs to.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And regardless of whether the policy was always carried out perfectly, was it the policy of the Bosnian government to fight for a unified multi-ethnic Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whether that was the policy, I think, yes. But to tell you the truth, I was a soldier. I carried out orders by -- from my superiors, and I was convinced that I was fighting for the right cause. But I think that the policy was just as you mention it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. And --

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were my convictions as well, that in Bosnia and Herzegovina that we were creating, we were to be all equal, that it would be a multicultural state, that it wasn't important who belonged to which ethnic group but it was important to see what kind of a person somebody was and -- and what kind of results they were achieving and what their contribution to the society as a whole was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Very well. Would you mind going, please, to paragraph number 7. Now, if you would just -- just briefly read paragraph number 7, and I'll ask you to comment on that. Tell me when you've read it and --

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, this is better. If you could just make it a little smaller. This is good now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Tell me when you've read it.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. The Bosnian army at the time of the Zenica meeting was just past its first birthday; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think that Army Day was on the 15th of April. That is Army Day. So the 21st, the 22nd of August, I don't think that it was an important date or anything like that, other than the fact that this meeting was held at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And although the -- the old history of the beginnings of the army might be strained beyond what's relevant in this case, it still is the fact, isn't it, that in -- in August of 1993, when this conference was held, you had an army which was really a group of people in the process of becoming an army rather than an army which was functioning with mature structures of command and control well understood by all parties? Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We wanted to have an army that was as good as possible, but we didn't have a perfect army. It's true that there were problems, that there was a lot of personnel who carried out certain functions which they were not trained for. Even I wasn't trained for the duty of corps commander, but I was a commander of a corps. The level of training in the JNA was up to battalion level. We were doing certain operations at the level of a brigade; however, corps operations at that level was something that I only encountered during the war. The majority of people who were occupying certain positions, in particular company commanders, were in the process of being trained for that position. They were not well versed at that point in everything that they needed to know in order to be able to function at such a position.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'll just stop you there for one moment and I'll ask you for a brief comment not related to the officers but related to the men, and I'll perhaps guide the answer by putting a couple of short questions to you. Most of the soldiers in -- in the Army of Bosnia were volunteers and civilians to your knowledge; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But the majority had already been through training in the JNA through their regular military term of duty, so they did have some soldier's knowledge and training, the majority of them. However, there were some who were being trained in the course of the war. There were many very young men who had joined any kind of army ranks for the first time in their life.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: The problems referred to in paragraph 7 really arose out of the realities of the soldiers you had to work with and the officers you had to work with and, to make it a longer question still, out of the situation --

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: -- of war in which you were first forced to conduct your training and your planning.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... to paragraph number 9, please. Now, there's a reference there, in paragraph number 9, to difficulties of finance. Is it the fact that individual units often had to find their own money to buy weapons, clothing, and food?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that they had to, but it's true that individuals did that. I don't know whether they had to. There were many who left the country and conducted various fund-raising activities and returned to the country and then used that money the way they felt it had to be used, evading any possibility of any kind of monitoring from the state or the military. So these were not just certain events or individual occurrences, but it was something that happened. It was ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Is it correct to say that there was an irregular flow of ammunition and weaponry to your units?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the exact situation in the army overall. I know what the situation was in the Neretva River Valley, in the area of Visoko. In the units where I was in command, I know that there was very little ammunition, not too many explosive devices. The artillery that I had at my disposal had perhaps one or two projectiles, not more than five according to each model. I never had more than five at a time. The ammunition reserves were -- well, it's true that there was an ammunition factory in Konjic; however, in 1993 -- I can't say it definitely that it was the only source of ammunition for -- to supply the units, but it was a very important one. It was a crucial facility for the resupply of infantry ammunition, as we called it. It was under the direct control of the Supreme Command Staff. The raw materials required for the production of this ammunition was seized in combat from HVO forces. I don't have all the information, but I think this was one of the main sources of supply for ammunition, particularly in the second half of 1993. It's true that we had very scarce material and equipment at our disposal and that is why the use of those -- or the allocation of those funds and the equipment was in the hands of very, very few people, who then had a lot of influence because of that. May I just add for purposes of comparison: When I, on the 20th of January, 1994, handed over my duty as corps commander, I told General Drekovic -- I presented to him an open casket of ammunition. When I say "open," it means that it wasn't full, a couple of boxes of 7.2 millimetres, one or two projectiles for tanks, and Howitzers, and I also gave him about 500.000 German marks. This means that I did have money but I didn't have ammunition. That was the situation before then also.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you very much, Mr. Gusic. I'm sorry, and I'm not cutting you off because you're going outside the question, I just -- I just want to focus on something else now and thank you for what you said. Mr. Gusic, would you look now, please, at paragraph number 10.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, you see that Rasim Delic has given expression to a concern that the -- the local media in Bosnia was not popularising the struggle and that it's -- that the media's professionalism and principles and patriotism were, at least at this stage of Zenica, more damaging than useful to the Bosnian army. Now, noticing that there, did you understand what the -- what Mr. Delic -- I'm calling him Mr. Delic -- what Commander Delic wanted was that the media engage more, if you like, proactively and positively in covering combat operations of the Bosnian army?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know what he wanted in this paragraph; meaning General Delic. But he probably wanted to have this issue popularised through the media, in terms of the real situation out in the front and in creating conditions for the military to have the correct and proper information rather than some distorted information, because there was a lot of distortion in the media regarding the situation. You could not trust and believe the media to the extent that you should have been able to do that, and he felt that the media should convey authentic information instead of adapting it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, he was going a bit further than that, wasn't he? He was suggesting that they should boost morale as well. Just having a look at the paragraph there.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're putting me in a particular situation. I do not wish to comment on the positions and orders of my commander. From the point in time of now, I would not write something like that, looking at it from today's point of view. But at that time, perhaps I would have written something like that. But today, when I look at this and when I view the media now, I think it is not all right to do this. The media, their role is not to improve or raise morale. It is up to the organisation, the superior officers, the development of positive qualities amongst all members of the army. That's how we should raise morale. So the media should really present information from close by or a little further off, information as they perceive it to be, but it should also be fair and correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Gusic. Could I ask you to go to number 3 now, point 3. And can you confirm that there under the heading of "Tasks," Commander Delic allocated the task to all corps, which presumably included yours, the 6th Corps, that "Offensive action shall be applied to a greater extent than before." In other words, he was encouraging a greater amount of offensive actions.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Would you go, please, to number 4. And can you confirm there that Commander Delic -- Mr. Gusic, I've just had a --

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Would you just excuse me one moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: At number 4, Commander Delic was making it quite clear that there needed to be a greater coordination of services, both civilian and military, in the service of the army.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could I please just look at that part of the text.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's point 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. Sorry, well, just to conclude, do you agree with the comment --

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says here in this point, but I wish to express my opinion about this. This is a matter of politics into which I never entered. I perhaps took note of this, but I was a soldier. I don't know how much it had to do with me. You might do better to put this question to someone who was working on the connection between politics and the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Well, we might. Thank you very much for the suggestion, Mr. Gusic. Well, thank you for that. And would you go, please, to paragraph number 9.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I've already commented on this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: No, it's -- sorry, pardon me. We now have a -- could the page please be turned over to the following page.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, we should be under the heading of Roman numeral II, "Tasks," here. There we have it. It's correctly on my screen now. But I still need it to go over to the next page after that. Thank you. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Do you now have at paragraph number 9 one that concerns a number of colourful military units?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Can you confirm that in -- at task number 9, Commander Delic made it clear that the previous small independent units which are named there should be attached to corps and effectively brought into the line of command under the organic control of corps?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And it chanced to be your good fortune that in your area of operations all of the mentioned units there were to be found; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was what I asked, that this be solved. I asked that this issue be solved at the meeting, but it wasn't solved at the meeting. It was left to be solved by some new order.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. And in fact, when you turn to the -- to the order that was issued by Commander Delic later on, on the 1st of September, when he purported to resubordinate certain units, your understanding is that he was doing so pursuant to this resolution or conclusion from Zenica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Would you just consider a couple of those units. The Crni Labudovi - I'm sorry about my pronunciation there - that's a unit called the Black Swans, the Crni Labudovi; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Were they a particularly well-dressed and well-paid for unit of soldiers?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had uniforms that were a bit better, but as to whether they were paid or not, I don't know. I don't know whether anyone was paid by these units. I did not have access to that information. I have never seen any proof that anyone received any kind of remuneration in any of these units. But they did have better equipment --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... what you say. I'm sorry. I'm sorry, that was an unfair question, to ask you what you didn't know. But let me just press on. That unit, the Black Swans, never actually came under the effective control of the 6th Corps after this time, did it?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never. Never completely. Because I could never go to that unit to analyse the situation in it, to influence appointments made within that unit, to use the entire unit as I wanted. No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And I'm just stepping outside of this document for a moment to ask you a more general question: Is it the case that in the Bosnian army at that time you could have all sorts of orders being issued which on their face looked as if they were binding but which the units on the ground just simply disregarded?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't agree with you, but I wouldn't say that there were not orders that were not carried out. Most of the units of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina carried out the orders they received. However, there were individual units protected by certain lobbies, and these units could not be commanded to the extent that was felt to be necessary. That did happen. The units you listed, all of those units, belonged to this latter category. Behind each of these units there was a lobby protecting it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Let me ask you a question about the Akrepi unit. Were they based in Konjic?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And after the Zenica meeting and leading up to -- and up until November the 1st, did the Akrepi unit remain based in Konjic?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I've got a question about the Zulfikar Unit. The Zulfikar Unit was commanded by Zulfikar Alispago; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And that was a unit which was keen to preserve its independence from the command of any particular corps; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That unit claimed to be directly under the staff of this Supreme Command and they even included that in their title, that they were under the Supreme Command Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. And could you tell the Tribunal here what's the -- the acronym. Is it PNSO that they would write next to their name to indicate that?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: SOPN SVK.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I had it wrong. But thank you for that. Very well. Could you go to point number 10. Do you have point number 10?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And in particular, I'm most interested in the boundary - it's the last -- it's the last subparagraph - the boundary between the 6th Corps and the 4th Corps. Correct? Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: That boundary was --

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: -- readjusted by virtue of this -- this document; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. For the forthcoming combat activities. That's why it was changed. The area of responsibility for combat operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Could I ask you to look at another map, please. And I just ask for the assistance of the court usher in this regard.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I just wonder -- before that's been placed on the device, I wonder if the witness could be asked to read out the title of that map. Perhaps he could just have the map -- the title displayed to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Gusic, I'd just ask you to look at the title of that map and indicate what that says. You may need to look on the other side as well.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Conclusions and assignments from the meeting in Zenica, August 1993, number 1/297-230 of the 29th of August, 1993, document number 01831684, Defence number 11."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Morrissey, does it have a MFI on it?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Would Your Honour excuse me for a minute, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be MFI134, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: MFI134, Your Honours. I'm grateful for the assistance which I've been given.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Are we going to see the map on the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: What I had in mind -- the Prosecutor is right to have asked the question. The witness is just inspecting it. I've indicated to the court usher a particular part that I would like shown, and I ask now that that be shown to the witness and the Court.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Gusic, I'm going to ask you to comment on that map in just a moment. But does that appear to you to be a map drawn to reflect the changes brought about by the decision at Zenica?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the first time I've seen this map, and since you let me read the title, the date appearing on the map is a bit odd. It's not clear to me why the writing is a bit thinner -- the line is a bit thinner than the remaining text on the map, if you look at it here. I'm not going into it, but this is the first time I've seen this map. And as for your question, in connection with the area of responsibility, it's like any other map. If you had brought me a blank map to draw in what it says here, I would probably do it in the same way.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, does it appear to you on the face of the map who -- by any initials who drafted that map -- oh, sorry. Pardon me. I'm instructed that -- not to worry about that. Pardon me, Mr. Gusic. Well, just have a look at that map and tell me if it accurately depicts the -- sorry, the redrafting of your boundaries as agreed in the light of Zenica.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'd have to check it against the text you let me read previously, but -- let me just have a look.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Have a look at the area of --

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Does that accurately reflect the area of operations and the zone of operations of the 6th Corps after the Zenica meeting?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the area of the village Gornja Grabovica, it does not reflect the area of responsibility of the 6th Corps because there should have been a sign like this one here. The way it appears at Plocno [phoen], Zeleno, indicating whether it's inclusive or exclusive. In Grabovica -- you can't see from this whether Grabovica is included or excluded. As this is on a communication, it had to be defined, whether it was included in the area of responsibility of the 6th Corps or whether it was excluded from the zone of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Morrissey, maybe you could ask the witness which side is the zone of responsibility of the 6th Corps on this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Well, you heard the question from His Honour. Which side is the zone of responsibility on that map and where do you say the 6th Corps' zone of responsibility actually began?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the upper side.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. And looking at that map, is it the fact that the houses, the small black dots of houses that are marked at Grabovica, do rather appear to fall within your zone of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. The village as such has to be clearly defined. It has to be defined who it belongs to, whether to the 6th Corps or to the 4th Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Mr. Gusic --

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because you see, I can draw the same kind of map leaving out the houses and --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. Mr. Gusic, if you're not persuaded by the map, could I please read to you your own words from the statement that I took you to earlier on, the 11th of the 3rd, 1999: "I learned of the events that took place in Grabovica after it all happened. Although it happened in the 6th Corps's area of responsibility, the forward command post was responsible for disciplinary offences committed by soldiers who were under the command of the command post and officers who established the forward command post." Now, do you agree that your position in the past had nothing to do with this resubordination to the 4th Corps but at the time you made that statement your explanation was that the incidents took place under the direction of the forward command post?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The incident I still think is something that the forward command post had to take care of, but as for the area of responsibility and the position of the village of Grabovica, this line that has been drawn here is the way it is. However, none of the villages in the area was in the zone of responsibility of the 6th Corps because the order --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... sorry. May I stop you. Therefore, do you renounce relying on the account that this village was in the zone of the 4th Corps?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The village was in the area of responsibility of the 4th Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Morrissey, if you don't mind, could I ask a question to this witness. Witness, suppose there is a forward commander post. Would you please point out for us where it is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This road in Jablanica here, this is the crossroads, and these buildings here. This is where the hydroelectric power plant in Jablanica is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may proceed, Mr. Morrissey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Although it's out of order, in response to His Honour's question, I might just ask you a question about that. When you went to visit the IKM -- and could I just ask you this question: You know what an inspection team is, don't you?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know what the inspection team is. I know that today. And the questions were --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... if you know what an inspection team is, do you know what the official name for the office whilst on the terrain of an inspection team is?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The official name for an inspection team?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: The office -- sorry, I must have misled you there, so I'll ask the question again. What I'm asking is the official name, the proper name, for the office of an inspection team when it's out in the field.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The area of deployment of the inspection team. Although, the inspection team never formed any such thing because they didn't have the elements for that. They usually relied on the elements of the combat disposition of the unit where they were; otherwise, they would have had to have their own security, logistics, communications, and so on in order to function and work normally if they did not rely on the units already existing in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Well, this does come to the question asked by His Honour: The fact is that the inspection team did not have any of those things within the -- within the inspection team at all; is that correct? But had to rely upon whatever it could get from local units.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether it did or not, but it set up a command post which did have all this. They had their premises. They had their communications centre, their security. I don't know how the food was provided. I don't know how it functioned. But they had many of the elements that a forward command post has to have, the essential ones. I'm not trying to say they had everything necessary, but they had the essentials.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Do you -- you know Bahrudin Fazlic, Braco; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bahrudin? He was my deputy.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: That's correct. I just want to put something. He indicates that you on the 8th of September went -- I'll read from it rather than paraphrasing it: "On the 8th of September, before the start of the operation, Commander Salko Gusic told me" --

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm not sure where counsel is reading from.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Pardon me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: My apologies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You have to lay down the foundations for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Well, what I'm proposing to put to the witness is a comment of his deputy. If there's no objection, I'll proceed with it. If there's an objection to it, then I won't frankly. So sorry, pardon me -- if there's -- I didn't know if I took it if there was an objection or not there, Your Honour. If that was an objection --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: No, no, no. I don't regard it as an objection but just to clarify what the source --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: What the document is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, the source of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Pardon me. Well, this is a statement provided to the Defence by the Prosecution of Bahrudin Fazlic, F-a-z-l-i-c, and it's dated the 27th of May, 2003. It's an interview with Bernard Brun, investigator, and we're referring here to paragraph 14 of that document.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Your Honour, now I would object. I don't think it's an appropriate procedure to be quoting from statements of -- of other people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: It's not evidence at this point, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, the witness gives a piece of the evidence. I believe that the party doing the cross-examination could use whatever material to challenge that kind of piece of the documents, which is the practice in this Tribunal for every other cases. Why not in our case that we should not allow them to do so? I just wonder, you know, what's the reason for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, could I just indicate this: My learned friend and I have had --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: There must be an issue of relevance, of reliability, of probative value, you know. Only out of these three conditions the Trial Chamber will bar any document to be used in the proceedings. Otherwise, I believe that the Defence team could use whatever documents they have.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honour, could I indicate in fairness to the Prosecutor, I understand her objection. There have been some discussions between us about the way in which we're going to use these statements because there's so many witnesses not being called. I'll continue those discussions, and what I'll do now is to hear the comment by my friend. I also hear what Your Honour's ruling is, but I'm going to content myself to putting some facts to the witness and seeing what he says. So I withdraw that question now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Mr. Gusic, I'm sorry about that departure into the land of statements, but now I'll -- I'll now put some propositions to you. On the 8th of September, did that -- that IKM in the hydro power plant consist of one big conference room with one telephone set, looking empty, not looking like a command post, and lacking -- generally speaking, lacking the facilities that you'd normally associate with a forward command post?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what it looked like to my deputy, but what I saw down there looked to me like quite a decent place, because my own command place was no better. It was no better furnished and equipped, and we used the facilities we found there. We didn't have any special facilities. And my command post was in the office of the director of an enterprise. I draw no special distinctions between one such facility and another. I don't want to say --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... I'm sorry. But there's a question I want to ask you about that. When you say you don't draw any distinctions between them, the fact is your corps command had a proper staff, with all the branches that are attached to a staff, security, communications, morale, intelligence, and all the other organs; correct? And if the question is: If that's correct, did you see any such organs attaching to this IKM?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You interrupted me just as I was about to say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: My apologies.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It seems that we are beginning to think alike. I don't want to say anything improper and say that they had all the elements I had at my command post, but they did have a building. They were able to establish communications. They had a far better trained staff than I had, because they had experienced officers. The forward command post, when it is established, doesn't have to reflect fully the structure of the command. It is only the essential officers that are brought to a forward command post, and I think that they were brought there. All the people I saw there - and I still think this today - were the best trained and most professional men in the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina and the forward command post could function with them there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... who was in charge of the military police of that IKM?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you're asking me as if I was there at that command post. I don't know that --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... if you weren't there, were there any military police at that command post?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I visited that place, what I noticed was that that security was conducted by members of the special purpose unit, the Zulfikar Unit. What I saw at the entrance, at the entry gates, that's what I saw. I saw people from that unit. And I think that they were performing security functions in that location.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. And the communications by the IKM was performed - and I'm using the term "IKM" as you do -- because you do - the communications functions were those of the 44th Jablanica Brigade, which was a local unit based in Jablanica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You could see that from the initial documents, because in the heading obviously when the first documents were sent out, you could see the "44th Brigade" in the heading and then below that it was the "IKM order." That's what you could see on the documents. Very soon after that you had in the heading "The IKM" only. In the very beginning, yes, but afterwards the IKM used its own documents and its own headings in correspondence within and outside of the command post.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Could the witness please be shown a document, DD00.0278. It's 65 ter number D73. And it's MFI, marked for exhibit MFI135. While that's being produced, could I offer the map which was shown to the witness and is sitting next to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, of course. And -- but you have to tell us what's the source of this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Well, it's -- that map is in fact a document drafted contemporaneously by a witness who is present in court by permission of the Court, Mr. Dzambasovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We'll deal with admission issues at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Do you have in front of you now a document which is --

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you just please zoom in a little bit. Excellent. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. Now, are you able to see that that's an order setting up a IKM?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Would you please scroll the document up. I just want to see the bottom of the document. I've already read the heading. Could you roll it down a little bit so that I could see from that place "I order." Can you put that at the top, the word that says "Naredujem," and then I want to see the text below that. Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. Could we continue to see the following page to that one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now, on the second page, you see that this is an order from many months before what we're talking about from Sefer Halilovic at the time when he was the commander of the army; correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am seeing this document for the first time in this form, and I see that somebody signed for the general.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Yes. I understand you haven't -- I'm not suggesting that you have seen it. I'm really showing it to you as an example and to make some points arising out of the form of the document bearing in mind the question asked by His Honour earlier on. Now, could we -- having looked at that, do you see that it's signed on behalf of Sefer Halilovic? Correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No audible response]

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. Could we now return, please, to the first page, again. Could I indicate, Mr. Gusic, and perhaps also to the Court that the reason for taking time on this matter is that -- the nature of the term "IKM" can be of interest and issue in this case, and that's why I'm asking the questions in some level of detail. Very well. Would you just look now, please, and note this: That this IKM is established by an order; correct? Because of the words "I hereby order"; do you agree?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Do you also agree that this order sets out in detail the responsibilities of various individuals connected with the IKM established under the order?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can say that it speaks about specific responsibilities, but it does delineate the areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. Well, that will suffice. And do you agree - and you can look at the document as much as you want - that there is no commander of the IKM appointed or listed in that document? And you can look from the top to the bottom.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this part I see that there isn't one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: By all means, look on the following page if you need to.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's no need.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... ask you a couple of other questions. An IKM is not a commanding body but a place, a location; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The IKM, the way it's used, is "istureno komandno mesto," "forward command post." That's a location. That's true. But a forward command post in the combat order is a place from which command is carried out. It's a place --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... your answer is relevant, but I want to test you about something there. You say that the -- a forward command post may, when it's in a combat area, be of a different nature. But what I'm putting to you, just to be clear about it, is that the forward command post itself is merely a location to which the commander may come. Is that correct?
