utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The command post is just a location. It's all locations. So you are right. Not only the IKM, but also the command post, the communications centre. The communications centre is also a location because when the equipment is brought into the communications centre, then it starts performing its functions. But until then, it's just a location.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: But a -- an IKM will continue to be an IKM -- well, first of all, I should take a step back. This IKM that's -- that's referred to in the document in front of you is a location in Zenica. It is located in Zenica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. And that IKM being -- being created by order, continues to be an IKM and to operate even when there's no one there at the IKM who's got commanding power; is that correct? In other words, if the typists are there and if a couple of staff officers are there working away, that IKM continues to exist but there's no one there who's got any commanding power; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After such an order until an order is issued to abolish that IKM, the IKM continues to exist.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And just because somebody is the most senior person at an IKM, that doesn't mean that -- sorry. That doesn't mean that that person has got any command power; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a question that depends on the specific situation. If the person is sitting there at the IKM and is not doing anything, then this is correct what you are asking. But if that person is sitting at the IKM but is conducting certain activities from the IKM, then that person is in command of the IKM.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And in short, of course it's the case that if a commander comes to the forward command post, then they remain the commander and they give their orders. That's correct, isn't it? It may sound tremendously self-evident, but I just ask you to answer it. It's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The rules of service define who is senior and who is subordinate. Whenever a superior appears, they take over the command role.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Now -- well, I'm going to ask you questions about that on Monday. But the point is this: Just because a person is based at an IKM, you cannot infer from that fact alone that they themselves have any particular commanding function. Rather, you must look to the terms of the order granting them whatever authority they have. Now, do you agree with that proposition?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand. Who is supposed to look at the terms of the responsibility or authority? Is the one who's receiving the orders from that person or the person themselves?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'm actually thinking of the -- of the Tribunal here, Mr. Gusic. Let me put a more concrete example, if that -- if that might assist. The question of whether Sefer Halilovic was or was not in command of a particular operation is not to be determined by reference to his presence or otherwise in a location called an IKM by, rather, is to be inferred or established by reference to the orders, if they exist, appointing him commander. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: General Halilovic and General Delic or any other of my superiors could not come -- could have come to my command post and at the time they were there they could have issued a binding order to me. But a presence at the command post does not imply that they had taken over a command of an operation and its entire course. Unless there is an order indicating such a thing and if they did not actively take part in operations, their presence at the command post does not necessarily mean that they are the person who is commanding the forces, unless they are actually making some command decisions and conducting the command duties.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. I understand, Mr. Gusic. And in short, in order just to determine the scope of Mr. Halilovic's command responsibilities in law, I take it what you say is this: We need to look to the orders which granted him any such authority.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: I object to the -- I'm very hesitant to get on my feet and disturb counsel, but again, the same objections as last time on the characterising of the law.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I agree with you on this aspect. Maybe you could put your question another way.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Or maybe you'll drop it, because the question is too obvious to ask this, you know, witness to answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I shall drop it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Gusic. Very well. Could the witness please be shown the third page of this document which is on the screen. Mr. Gusic, the further page is going to be shown to you in a minute.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. If you could just enlarge it a little bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Gusic, what's being shown to you here -- could I just indicate, lest you notice with surprise which army this comes from. This is a document that I'm showing for the same reason as the last one, but it's a document of the Army of the Republika Srpska, so it's not a document directly from the Bosnian army. But it may be that the form of it is sufficiently similar for you to notice the things I want to point out and you can make any comment that you want to if you think that the fact of it coming from the Republika Srpska interferes with its value. First of all, does this appear to you to be another order establishing an IKM?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... All right. I'll come up with some more examples of the form of this order in a moment. But I just want to ask you a more general question which might assist the Court: The term IKM, as it's translated in English, "Forward command post," describes a derivative command place which implies the existence of a primary command post. In other words, a commander has a command post, and he may have a variety of other small posts, IKMs, forward command posts, or rear command posts, or other types of command posts. I understand that's not perhaps put in acceptable military terminology, but is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Yes, it is. But there is just one thing: Earlier I was not sure whether I should or shouldn't ask you. Very well. I would rather comment like this on documents which are not documents of my commander or my superiors. I don't think that I am capable or called upon to comment on the documents of my commanders and my other superiors. But in the form that you are doing it, all the commanders were in the position to form IKMs in order to have a more easier manner of commanding their compositions and their units.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. I'm sorry, just so that I understand there, are you -- if you say you're uncomfortable looking at Republika Srpska documents like that, I won't put it to you, because it's really just meant to help. Are you happy to look at this document or not?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The documents of Republika Srpska do not bother me at all. But when we're talking as we are, I would rather comment on this rather than the documents by my commanders. My superior was General Halilovic and General Delic. So I would rather not comment on such documents. This order here is written in accordance with the rules and regulations in force in the JNA, and then this -- these rules and regulations continue to be used in the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Mr. Gusic, thank you for that clarification. I -- I fear that I'll be putting questions to you that -- that might indicate that you and I are not thinking along the same path any more in the future. But, however, we'll leave those for -- for Monday. And now I want to continue with these questions about the IKM. You raised a point a minute ago of interest, and that was that it's within the power of a commander from his command post to designate another area as his forward command post if he chooses.

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No audible response].

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, on the theory that Sefer Halilovic was the commander of Neretva 93, where do you say his command post was?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: His command post was at the forward command post, the IKM, of the Supreme Command Staff out in the field at the location. We said that the IKM is a location, so his command post was at that location.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. But the existence -- I want to put this proposition to you. Mr. Gusic, you understand that this is accepting for a moment your thesis about the existence of the forward command post. If it was the case that Sefer Halilovic was at a forward command post in Jablanica, where's the main command post of which the forward command post is a derivative location?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The main command post of the Army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina was always in Sarajevo, the main command post.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... commander of the army at that location, other than Rasim Delic?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot really talk about the positions at different time periods.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... at -- you know what we're talking about here. We're talking about at the time of this IKM. Now, what I'm putting to you is: Rasim Delic was the commander of the army in Sarajevo at that time. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't. Because there's an order signed by General Siber. At the time General Siber was at the position of being the most responsible person at the main command post in Sarajevo. He -- General Siber signed the order to cease combat operations. At the time, he was the one who issued that order which was binding on all of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. But just a moment. General Siber -- you're referring to a time when -- Mr. Gusic, aren't you referring to a time when -- when General Delic was in Geneva and Siber was acting as his deputy and signing documents as his deputy? Isn't that the fact?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know where General Delic was. Probably he was in Geneva, like you said. But it is a fact that General Siber issued orders on his behalf.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Mr. Gusic, I think -- I put it to you earlier that you and I were going to part company again at a later time on the existence of the IKM, but what I'm putting to you now is this: On your theory that Sefer Halilovic is the commander of the IKM, that institution in Jablanica was no IKM at all but a KM, a command post of the primary and basic kind; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise to the general and to my commanders, my superiors, but you're putting me again in the position of having to comment on what they called what. I am not dealing with how they called certain things. I know what the heading on the documents was and the orders which I, amongst others, received, and it said on that order "forward command post of the Supreme Command Staff Jablanica." Based on that order, based on the fact that I was there and in the admin building of the thermoelectric power station, I came to the conclusion that there was a forward command post, an IKM, from where the forces of -- during the Neretva operation - I know that now, but I didn't know that up until a while ago - were commanded. So we're talking about the active combat operations conducted towards Mostar and Prozor.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Bearing in mind the -- the detail on the document that you're looking now, the order forming the IKM, and the previous document that you looked at, forming the IKM at Zenica, would you indicate what document you say forms the IKM which you claim existed at Jablanica. I'm not talking here about documents that refer to it. I'm talking here about a document that forms it, that establishes an IKM. And perhaps I should ask you in fairness: Do you know whether any such document exists?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You don't have to put an honest question to me, but I will give you an honest answer. I was not in a position to be given such a document unless I had some duties in relation to the formation of such a combat entity. I never saw a document in which it's -- which stated that a forward command post was being formed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I understand that. What you'd say is somewhere in the archives or somewhere in history there was such a document forming this IKM but you've quite understandably never seen it? Is that your position?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that such a document existed. I believe that. When I say "I believe that," it doesn't mean that I assert that. Because it's much easier to work if certain things are specified in the proper time, then it is much easier to set up certain -- a certain organisation or an order of things. But I never saw such a document and probably since I didn't see it, there was no need for me to see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I understand what you say, Mr. Gusic. Can I just ask you one -- I note the time is now creeping --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, could I indicate -- do you intend to finish at 7.00?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, you have to understand it's a Friday afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We have to stop. We have to stop at 7.00 sharp.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I must indicate that it's learned counsel for the Defence's birthday and whose children have demanded that he stop at 7.00, and I'd be grateful if -- I'd be very grateful to comply with standard practice. Could I just ask a couple more questions before 7.00?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, before 7.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, definitely.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Mr. Gusic, the final questions are about an -- about the use of the term "IKM." I want to put something to you here. Experienced officers might -- well, what I want to put to you is something different. Experienced officers in this case did refer to the Jablanica post as an IKM and that that term was used in documents from time to time and it was also used, I suppose, in discussion from time to time. But what I'm suggesting is to you: You can't rule out the possibility that that use of the term "IKM" was an imprecise use and that it was used in a shorthand way to describe the location of the team that came down from Sarajevo in the absence of an official term for an inspection team's office. What do you say to that proposition?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't agree with you. I have a right to disagree with that. Why? Had you put that question to me without my having seen certain documents, I probably would have said that that is all right. But if there was no need to change the heading, why was the change -- the heading changed from the beginning which contained the name of the 44th Brigade? So probably there was a need to change the heading because from the document and the signatories of the document you could see that this was from the -- a document from members of the Supreme Command Staff. You could see who the signatory was. If that was the thing, then, again, there was the possibility of saying "IKM" in the heading and then put the name of the brigade or -- or the corps there also. What you are saying right now is something that I cannot wholly agree with, no. Although, I am not disputing it totally. But I cannot fully agree with what you are saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I take it your position is it's possible but you are not -- not prepared to assert it yourself. Is that a correct analysis of your position?

utterances.speaker: SALKO GUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. It's possible, but you were speaking about practice. We're talking about practice. And this is something that is clearly defined, that you could use a heading -- you didn't have to emphasise the IKM. You could use the heading -- the standard heading used by the chief in Sarajevo. It didn't have to contain the term "IKM." The one who sent it to the IKM would know where the document is coming from. Finally, if the Jablanica communications centre was used, then you would know it came from Jablanica. So if that institution didn't exist, there would have been no need to change the heading. Why this was done is something that I would not really speculate about, but in my opinion it was possible not to change it as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Except for this though - and this is the last question I'll put to you for the evening - that once that -- once that location had achieved the popular name of -- of being the IKM among people working in the area, it would have caused more trouble than it was worth to change it. Do you agree with that possibility?

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: That's speculative, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Mr. Morrissey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: It's a speculative question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I must say it was speculative.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I think, you know, we have to stop at this moment, and I believe that the cross-examination has a point in it, but the question is that, you know, how to make it more concise, you know. Maybe during the weekend, you know, the Defence team could reorganise a little bit their strategy, you know, in this way. And at the same time, you know, I have to remind the witness that most of the questions put to you by the Defence counsel could be answered by simply saying yes or no. If the Defence counsel need more information, there will be, I guess, follow-up questions to you. And at this stage I also remind you what I said yesterday because I'm afraid that we have to keep you in The Hague for the weekend. Yes, Mr. Morrissey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just thought as a matter of courtesy to the witness and also to the Court to indicate that the cross-examination is unlikely to be completed at the end of Monday. Every attempt is going to be made to streamline it. But as I indicated, the Prosecution has decided to -- frankly, to put a fair amount of its case through this witness, as they did. And therefore, the witness is going to be pressed on a number of matters which have been led through him, and therefore I see it as likely - and this may assist for scheduling of witnesses - as likely that the cross-examination would go into Tuesday but leaves the possibility of some time for a witness on Tuesday. In any event, we undertake to be finished by the time that the videolink witnesses are to be scheduled, which I believe to be later in the week, on a fixed date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, thank you very much for your information. I understand that this witness is a very important to both parties, so we did not strictly limit the time of the direct examination or cross-examination. But anyway, we have to make the best use of the time available to us and try to -- try your best during the weekend to, you know, make it shorter. Well, having said that, I wish everybody a happy weekend. We will see you Monday morning in the same courtroom. The hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 7th day of February, 2005, at 9.00 a.m.
